issues.failure_explanation: For x in M, Cx need not lie in L. With H=F, A=0, B=diag(1,0), C=I_2, M=F^2, L=span(e_1), and Cx is not in L for x=e_2, so the claimed injective map and dimension argument are invalid.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proof of part 2, and therefore the derivation of part 3, with a valid proof of Frobenius's inequality for Bochner matrices, e.g. by a correct kernel/image dimension argument; the statements can remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The Frobenius inequality and the Sylvester consequences are not established as written; later rank, factorization, SVD, pseudoinverse, and cross-approximation results relying on them are unsupported until this proof is repaired.
issues.title: Frobenius inequality proof uses an invalid injective map
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained replacement of a faulty standard linear-algebra proof, not a change of the main claims, but it is more than a one-line routine correction because the source's argument is structurally invalid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the \scup{adjoint} of $\Bmatrix{A} \in \Hilb^{m \times n}$ as a linear operator $\Bmatrix{A}^\ast : \Hilb^{m} \to \F^{n}$,

the ``product'' $\Bmatrix{C} \Bmatrix{A}^\ast$ stands for the composition of linear operators $\mul{\Bmatrix{C}} \circ \Bmatrix{A}^\ast$, where $\mul{\Bmatrix{C}}: \Matrix{x} \mapsto \Bmatrix{C}\Matrix{x}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For general Hilbert spaces, A E^* is not a defined product under the established conventions: E^*: H^n -> F^l, whereas A: F^n -> H^m. Also (A^* D)^* has type F^{k x n}, while columnwise D^* A has type F^{m x n}; the proof indexes the two as the same matrix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or correct the last two identities, or introduce a properly typed dual-matrix product and reprove them; the first two identities and downstream uses of only those can be preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's last two adjoint manipulation identities are invalid or undefined; results using only the first identity are not necessarily affected.
issues.title: Adjoint-product lemma contains ill-typed identities
issues.why_classification: This is a substantive type/convention failure in a formal lemma, but a limited repair by weakening or restating the affected identities avoids changing the paper's main architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To prove uniqueness, suppose that linear operators $\Linop{B}$ and $\Linop{C}$ satisfy all four equations.

issues.failure_explanation: The Moore-Penrose equations give (A C)^* = C^* A^*, not B^* A^*. Replacing B^* A^* by (A C)^* = C^* A^* is unjustified, and the analogous step for C is likewise invalid; the proof does not establish B=C.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniqueness proof with a standard valid proof for the four Moore-Penrose equations (or derive uniqueness from the SVD construction); the theorem statement can remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The existence/uniqueness theorem for the Bochner Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse is not proved as written, leaving lemmas and cross-approximation identities that rely on A^dag unsupported.
issues.title: Pseudoinverse uniqueness proof has unjustified equalities
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained proof correction preserving the pseudoinverse theory, but the source's argument is not a routine algebraic omission; it relies on false substitutions.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition quantifies over usual Q and usual A and only asserts a left-invariance identity; it does not define invariance under Bochner left isometries or usual right unitaries. The proof nevertheless applies it with Bochner U and usual Sigma V^*, which is outside the stated definition.

failure_location.quote: We say that a norm $\Norm{\cdot}{\bullet}$ for Bochner matrices is \scup{unitarily invariant} if there exists a unitraily invariant norm $\Norm{\cdot}{\circ}$ for usual matrices such that $\Norm{\Bmatrix{Q} \Matrix{A}}{\bullet} = \Norm{\Matrix{A}}{\circ}$ for every $\Bmatrix{Q}$ with orthonormal columns.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the definition with a well-formed notion of unitarily invariant Bochner norm, e.g. invariance under Bochner column isometries and usual right unitaries together with an associated usual singular-value norm, and adjust the short proofs accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The central unitarily-invariant norm theorem, Mirsky extension, norm-equivalence corollary, closed-set corollary, one-sided projection optimality, and the HOSVD error statement for arbitrary such norms are unsupported by the definition as written.
issues.title: Unitarily invariant Bochner norm definition is not the one used
issues.why_classification: A natural corrected definition is locally supported by the paper's SVD framework and preserves the advertised Mirsky-type results, but the existing definition is mathematically incompatible with its use.

issues.failure_explanation: For F=C, \bar Q_\rho Q_\rho^T is the transpose/conjugate of the orthogonal projection Q_\rho Q_\rho^*, not an orthogonal projection. The Pythagorean decomposition in the proof requires an orthogonal projection onto the retained row subspace.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \overline{Q}_\rho Q_\rho^T by Q_\rho Q_\rho^* (or the corresponding adjoint projection) in the definition of B and in the proof; the intended bound then follows by the existing one-sided projection corollary.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Bochner HOSVD construction and its Frobenius error bound are invalid in the complex case.
issues.title: HOSVD uses the wrong complex projection
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local notation/complex-conjugation fix that preserves the stated HOSVD approximation result and rate.

issues.failure_explanation: G is |I| by |J|, while (G^T)^dag C^T is a usual |I| by m matrix. The displayed product G (G^T)^dag C^T is not conformable in general (in particular when |I| != |J|), and the asserted factorization C = ((G^T)^dag C^T)^T G is not derived from the preceding equation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the proof of (2 => 4), or if necessary restate the factorization with a properly typed usual row-selection matrix, and then rederive the cross-component identity.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence in the two-sided interpolative/cross decomposition lemma is not proved; cross_exact, which cites it, is unsupported.
issues.title: Two-sided CUR lemma has a non-conformable proof step
issues.why_classification: The lemma is central to the cross approximation machinery, but a contained proof repair can preserve the intended statement; it is not a false theorem with no supported correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $n_{\mathrm{rook}} = 0$, the rows are selected at random and the choice of columns is adaptive.

issues.failure_explanation: If n_rook=0, the for loop is not executed, i_* is never assigned, and the output pivot indices are undefined. The paper explicitly uses n_rook=0 as a meaningful regime, and ABCD calls this subroutine after choosing a random i_s that is not passed to rook.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a base case to rook (e.g. return the current row and column, or accept the current row as input) or handle n_rook=0 directly inside ABCD before calling rook.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised ABCD/ABCDX procedures are not well defined in the zero-rook regime used in the numerical discussion.
issues.title: Bochner rook pivoting is undefined for n_rook=0
issues.why_classification: A local pseudocode fix restores the advertised zero-rook behavior without changing the algorithm's mathematical guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: Substitution into the stated BVP gives denominators k^2 - alpha^2 and k^2 - beta^2, not k^2 + alpha^2 and k^2 + beta^2. For example, when beta=0 the sine coefficient is proportional to (1-(-1)^k)/(k(k^2-alpha^2)), not k/(k^2+alpha^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correct the differential equation or the Fourier coefficient formula and regenerate all reported numerical results for that experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The linear boundary-value experiment approximates the wrong solution map, so the numerical conclusions drawn from that experiment are unsupported.
issues.title: Fourier solution formula for the linear BVP is incorrect
issues.why_classification: The displayed solution is false for the stated problem, and the source does not provide corrected numerical evidence; the advertised validation experiment loses support unless the problem/formula and experiments are redone.
